name: Bondi-Sachs Radiating Metric
description: The form the metric of an isolated body that sends out gravitational waves takes in coordinates built on its outgoing light cones, given by Hermann Bondi, M. G. J. van der Burg, A. W. K. Metzner, and Rainer Sachs in 1962. In it the mass of the body falls for as long as news of a change in the body reaches infinity, and cannot rise.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and write every mass as a length, $G/c^2$ times the mass. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: On 14 September 2015 two black holes of 36 and 29 solar masses merged into one of 62, and three solar masses left as gravitational waves [abbott2016]. Where does a spacetime keep its mass, that a wave can carry some of it away? Through the 1950s relativists could not agree that a wave carried any [kennefick1999]. Leopold Infeld and his student Adrian Scheidegger had concluded that two stars in orbit about each other, each in free fall, lose no energy to waves [kennefick1999]. Hermann Bondi, who had learned relativity from Arthur Eddington's books and doubted that the waves existed, found Landau and Lifshitz's calculation of the loss "a little glib" [kennefick1999].¶By 1957 Bondi was convinced that a plane wave passing a detector leaves energy behind in it [bondi1957, hill2016]. A plane wave fills all of space and has no source, so the mass of a body that radiates was still an open matter [hill2016]. Andrzej Trautman, a student in Infeld's group, wrote down in 1958 boundary conditions for the gravitational field far from an isolated body that radiates, and showed that the energy leaving through them cannot be negative [trautman1958, hill2016, kennefick1999]. In May and June of that year he lectured on them at King's College London, with Bondi and Felix Pirani in the audience [hill2016].¶Bondi's approach, which he presented in 1960, was to build the coordinates out of the outgoing light itself: the retarded time $u$ is constant on each light cone leaving the source, two angles are constant along each ray, and the distance $r$ along the ray is fixed by giving the sphere of constant $u$ and $r$ the area $4\pi r^2$ [bondi1960, bondi1962, madler2016]. With M. G. J. van der Burg and A. W. K. Metzner he took a source with an axis of symmetry, for which the metric is $ds^2 = -\frac{V}{r}e^{2\beta}du^2 - 2e^{2\beta}du\,dr + r^2e^{2\gamma}\left(d\theta - U\,du\right)^2 + r^2e^{-2\gamma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$ with four functions of $u$, $r$, and $\theta$, and solved the vacuum equations in powers of $1/r$ [bondi1962]. Far from the source the wave is one function, $\sigma(u, \theta)$, with $\gamma = \sigma/r$ to leading order, and its rate of change is the news: "the flow of information to infinity is controlled by a single function of two variables called the news function", $\partial_u\sigma$ [bondi1962]. The mass is read from the next term of $V = r - 2M$, as the average of $M(u, \theta)$ over the sphere, $m(u) = \frac{1}{2}\int_0^\pi M\sin\theta\,d\theta$, and in units with $G = c = 1$ it obeys $\frac{dm}{du} = -\frac{1}{2}\int_0^\pi\left(\partial_u\sigma\right)^2\sin\theta\,d\theta$ [bondi1962, madler2016]. In their words, "the mass of a system is constant if and only if there is no news; if there is news, the mass decreases monotonically so long as it continues" [bondi1962]. Bondi's own verdict on the paper of 1962, in his autobiography, was "the best scientific work I have ever done, which is later in life than mathematicians supposedly peak" [madler2016].¶Rainer Sachs removed the axis of symmetry the same year, which adds a second polarisation and brings the functions to six: $ds^2 = -\frac{V}{r}e^{2\beta}du^2 - 2e^{2\beta}du\,dr + r^2h_{AB}\left(dx^A - U^A du\right)\left(dx^B - U^B du\right)$, where $h_{AB}$ has the determinant of the unit sphere's metric [sachs1962, madler2016]. He concluded that "gravitational waves appear to carry mass away from the interior" [sachs1962]. The coordinate changes that keep this form far from the source make up a group larger than Poincaré's, the Bondi-Metzner-Sachs group [sachs1962bms, madler2016]. Besides the Lorentz transformations and the four translations it holds the supertranslations, which shift $u$ by a different amount in each direction and are infinite in number [sachs1962bms, madler2016]. Roger Penrose then made infinity a place: with $\ell = 1/r$ as a coordinate and the metric multiplied by $\ell^2$, the far ends of the outgoing rays form a boundary at $\ell = 0$, future null infinity, where Bondi's series in $1/r$ is the statement that the rescaled metric is smooth [penrose1963, madler2016]. Ezra Newman and Penrose reached the same results with null tetrads and spin coefficients, in a notation so foreign to Bondi's that at meetings he would ask a colleague whether he was a qualified translator [newman1962, madler2016].¶Can a mass that only falls go below zero? The proof that the Bondi mass is positive came in 1982, from Richard Schoen and Shing Tung Yau and from Gary Horowitz and Malcolm Perry, so a body cannot radiate away more than it has [schoen1982, horowitz1982]. Which bodies have news to send stayed in dispute: at the Warsaw conference of 1962 Bondi argued that a binary made of dust without pressure, every particle in free fall, would have none, a view he later gave up [kennefick1999]. The binary pulsar of Russell Hulse and Joseph Taylor is two bodies in free fall, and Taylor and his coworkers measured its orbital period shrinking in line with the quadrupole formula [hulse1975, taylor1979, kennefick1999].¶The cones suit a computer as well: Richard Isaacson, J. S. Welling, and Jeffrey Winicour put the axisymmetric equations on one, marching outward along each null cone on a grid that reaches null infinity at a finite coordinate value [isaacson1983]. The waveform of a binary black hole merger is now computed at null infinity by Cauchy-characteristic extraction, which hands the data of a simulation to a code that carries it out along Bondi's cones [bishop1996, winicour2012]. A train of waves leaves free masses permanently displaced, an effect of the nonlinear theory that Demetrios Christodoulou found in 1991 [christodoulou1991]. Andrew Strominger and Alexander Zhiboedov showed that the positions before and after the waves differ by one of the supertranslations [strominger2016].

related.text: The member with $V = r - r_s$ and $\beta = \gamma = U = 0$, Schwarzschild's metric in outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates. It has no news, and its Bondi mass is the constant $r_s/2$, the mass Bondi's definition was made to agree with [bondi1962].

The member with $\beta = \gamma = U = 0$ and $V = r - 2Gm(u)/c^2$, a star that shines evenly [vaidya1953]. Its mass aspect is the same in every direction and falls as the light leaves, with no gravitational news.

Radiating vacuum spacetimes whose outgoing rays have no shear [robinson1962]. In Bondi's chart they have $\gamma = 0$, $e^{2\beta} = f$, and $U = \partial_\theta f/r$, with $f$ the function that shapes their wave fronts and $r$ their affine distance divided by $f$, a frame that is not inertial at infinity.

Kinnersley's rocket in its rectilinear chart is Bondi's metric with $\beta = \gamma = 0$, $U = -\alpha\sin\theta$, and $V = r - 2m - 2\alpha r^2\cos\theta$, with light in place of the vacuum [kinnersley1969]. Its news function vanishes, so it sends out no gravitational waves [cornish2000].

The member with $V = r$ and the other three functions zero, flat spacetime on its outgoing light cones. The coordinate changes that keep Bondi and Sachs's form far away make up a group larger than Poincaré's [sachs1962bms, madler2016].

A member of Sachs's general form with no news and a constant Bondi mass. Its rotation takes it outside Bondi's axisymmetric chart, which is unchanged by $\phi \to -\phi$, and S. J. Fletcher and A. W. C. Lun wrote it in generalised Bondi-Sachs coordinates in 2003 [madler2016, fletcher2003].

The plane waves of Bondi, Pirani, and Robinson are paper III of the series in which the radiating metric is papers VII and VIII [bondipirani1959, bondi1962, sachs1962]. A plane wave has no source, and these two papers gave the waves one.

Flat space with supertranslation hair, the member with no mass and a shear $\sigma(\theta)$ that never changes, so there is no news. With $W = \sqrt{r^2 + \sigma^2}$ it has $e^{2\beta} = r/W$ and $re^{\gamma} = W + \sigma$ [compere2016vacua].

coordinates.name: Bondi (axisymmetric)

parameters.description: Function with the dimension of a length that fixes $g^{rr}$. Far from the source $V = r - 2M + \dots$, where $M(u, \theta)$ is the mass aspect, a length, and the Bondi mass is its mean over the sphere, $m_B = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^\pi M\sin\theta\,d\theta$. In vacuum $V$ follows from $\gamma$, $\beta$, and $U$ by one integration along each ray, which no component assumes
Dimensionless function, with $e^{2\beta}dr$ the affine distance along an outgoing ray. In vacuum $\partial_r\beta = \tfrac{1}{2}r\left(\partial_r\gamma\right)^2$, which no component assumes

Function with the dimension of an inverse length, Bondi's $U$ and the one component $U^\theta$ of Sachs's $U^A$. In vacuum it follows from $\gamma$ and $\beta$ by two integrations along each ray, which no component assumes

Dimensionless function that fixes the shape of the sphere of constant $u$ and $r$, the one polarisation of an axisymmetric wave from a source that does not rotate. Far from the source $\gamma = \sigma/r + \dots$, where $\sigma(u, \theta)$ is the shear, a length, and $\partial_u\sigma$ is the news function. In vacuum $\partial_u\gamma$ on a cone follows from $\gamma$, $\beta$, $U$, and $V$ on it, which no component assumes

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$: the retarded time $u$, carrying dimensions of time, is constant on each outgoing light cone, $\theta$ and $\phi$ are constant along each ray of the cone, and $r$ is the luminosity distance, with $4\pi r^2$ the area of the sphere of constant $u$ and $r$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cu$, so $\partial_u$ means $c^{-1}\partial/\partial u$ and $\dot{u}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(cu)/d\lambda$. The metric does not depend on $\phi$ and is unchanged by $\phi \to -\phi$, so the source does not rotate.

In vacuum $V$ follows from $\gamma$, $\beta$, and $U$ by one integration along each ray, which no component assumes

Dimensionless function that fixes the shape of the sphere of constant $u$ and $\ell$, the one polarisation of an axisymmetric wave from a source that does not rotate. Far from the source $\gamma = \sigma\ell + \dots$, where $\sigma(u, \theta)$ is the shear, a length, and $\partial_u\sigma$ is the news function. In vacuum $\partial_u\gamma$ on a cone follows from $\gamma$, $\beta$, $U$, and $V$ on it, which no component assumes

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, \ell, \theta, \phi)$ with $\ell = 1/r$ the inverse of the luminosity distance, an inverse length, so that future null infinity is $\ell = 0$; $u$, carrying dimensions of time, $\theta$, and $\phi$ are those of Bondi's chart. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cu$, so $\partial_u$ means $c^{-1}\partial/\partial u$ and $\dot{u}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(cu)/d\lambda$. The metric is the physical one, and $\ell^2$ times it is the rescaled metric that is regular at $\ell = 0$.
